scope: Documentary record of the Prime Minister's Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations Fund (PM CARES Fund): (1) its constitution as a registered public charitable trust and the contested question of its status under the Right to Information Act 2005; (2) every Receipts and Payments Account the fund has published, with the years it has not published named explicitly; (3) announced allocations set against what the audited statements record; (4) the statutory route by which contributions became eligible CSR expenditure; and (5) the same analysis run on the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF) as a control. Descriptive only. No allegation of misappropriation, wrongdoing or improper intent against any person or institution is made or implied anywhere in this file. Where two official records disagree, both are carried and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved.
headline: The control result governs this file. On the two facts most often presented as PM CARES-specific - that it refuses RTI on the ground that it is not a 'public authority', and that its published accounts stop at FY2022-23 - the 1948 Prime Minister's National Relief Fund is identical, and took the RTI position first, in litigation that began in 2011 and reached a Delhi High Court Division Bench that split 1-1 on 23 May 2018, two years before PM CARES existed. Both funds are administered from the PMO by the same officers, were audited by the same firm (SARC & Associates), have both since appointed the same new firm (KKC & Associates LLP), and both publish a one-page Receipts and Payments Account with the accompanying notes withheld. Four of seven elapsed financial years are published by each. What survives the control is narrower and is set out in contested[] and control.departuresThatSurvive.

method.primaryFirst: Every financial figure in this file was read off a statement published by the fund itself on pmcares.gov.in or pmnrf.gov.in. Both funds publish their accounts as SCANNED IMAGES with no text layer (pypdf extracted 0 characters from the PM CARES FY2019-20, FY2020-21 and FY2021-22 PDFs and 69 characters from the two-page FY2022-23 PDF). Every page was therefore rasterised with pdftoppm at 200 dpi and read as an image. The trust deed (16 scanned pages, 26 MB) was read the same way at 150 dpi.
method.castingCheck: Every published column was re-added programmatically against its printed total. FY2022-23 casts exactly in both directions (receipts 67,23,06,78,171 and closing balance 62,83,68,30,782 both reproduce to the rupee). FY2020-21 and FY2021-22 do not cast to the rupee against the totals as I read them: the FY2020-21 receipts components sum to Rs 1,09,90,17,32,872 against a printed total of Rs 1,09,90,17,32,873, and the FY2021-22 payments components sum to Rs 37,16,29,43,077 against a printed total of Rs 37,16,29,43,076. In both cases the discrepancy is exactly Rs 1 and is far more likely to be a single misread digit on a scanned image than an error in the statement. The PRINTED TOTALS are carried as authoritative throughout; component figures are carried with this caveat attached and are flagged componentReadFromScan: true.
method.unpublishedYearsProbed: The absence of later statements was tested, not assumed. The fund's own About page indexes exactly four Receipts and Payments Accounts. The site's naming convention is Audited_Statement_YYYY_YY.pdf; requests for Audited_Statement_2023_24.pdf, Audited_Statement_2024_25.pdf and Audited_Statement_2023-24.pdf each returned HTTP 404. The About and FAQ pages both carry 'Last updated on: 10 August 2026', two days before this file's asOf.
method.control: The identical retrieval was run on PMNRF - a fund nobody framed as a transparency scandal until PM CARES existed - before any conclusion was drawn about PM CARES. Its About page, its PMNRF FAQ page and its FY2022-23 Receipts and Payments Account were all fetched and read.
method.courts: The Supreme Court judgment was taken from the Court's own server (api.sci.gov.in), not from a legal-database mirror; main.sci.gov.in did not resolve by DNS from this network but api.sci.gov.in served the same path. The Delhi High Court judgment in the PMNRF appeal was taken from delhihighcourt.nic.in itself. indiankanoon.org was not used.
method.statute: The amendment of Schedule VII of the Companies Act 2013 was read from India Code's official consolidated text of the Act (370 pages), which carries the amendment as a numbered footnote to the Schedule. mca.gov.in returns HTTP 403 to every automated request including its static /Ministry/pdf/ paths, so the MCA circulars themselves could not be read; the notification is nonetheless established at documented tier from the statute text.
method.nullPolicy: No figure, date, case number, question number or citation in this file is estimated, inferred or recalled. Anything not read off a fetched document is null with a note and a corresponding gaps[] entry. Claims sourced only to a news outlet are tiered reported and the outlet is named; no search-result snippet is cited as a source anywhere.
method.personsNamed: Only people acting in a public office or a public professional capacity are named: ex officio and nominated trustees, PMO officers who signed published accounts, the signing partner of the audit firm whose name and membership number are printed on documents published by the Government, judges, ministers and Members of Parliament. The residential addresses of the two witnesses printed on the registered trust deed are deliberately not reproduced.

deedKeyClauses.quote: This trust is established only for the charitable purposes incorporated in these presents and for the noble causes enumerated herein. This Trust is not created by or under the Constitution of India or by any law made by the Parliament or by any State Legislature. This Trust is neither intended to be or is in fact owned, controlled or substantially financed by any Government or any instrumentality of the Government. There is no control of either the Central Government or any State Government/s, either direct or indirect, in functioning of the Trust in any manner whatsoever. The composition of the Board of Trustees consisting of holders of public office ex officio is merely for administrative convenience and for smooth succession to the trusteeship and is neither intended to be nor in fact result into any governmental control in the functioning of the Trust in any manner whatsoever.
deedKeyClauses.why: These are the exact elements of the test in section 2(h) of the RTI Act 2005 - creation by Constitution, by law of Parliament, by law of a State Legislature, or a body owned, controlled or substantially financed by government - recited in the negative in the instrument itself. The recital is in the deed as executed and registered on 27 March 2020; nothing in the published document indicates it was inserted later. Whether the drafting anticipated the statutory test is not something the record settles.

deedKeyClauses.quote: the Trust shall fully respect and will not allow any invasion of the privacy of the contributor/s by divulging their names, addresses and/or other details and the details regarding their contributions to anyone except to the tax authorities while making the full and true disclosures which will be made to the tax authorities as and when required by such authorities or required under the relevant taxing statute.
deedKeyClauses.why: The non-disclosure of donor identities is a term of the trust instrument, not an administrative choice or a litigation position. Any expectation that donor lists will be published requires this clause to be overridden.

deedKeyClauses.quote: The Prime Minister's Office (PMO) shall provide such administrative and secretarial support to the Trustees for the management and administration of the Trust, as may be required by the Trustees including coordinating with the Advisory Board.

The account books so signed by the Trustees shall be examined, audited and certified once in each Financial Year and the audited statements of account shall be signed in accordance with applicable law and shall be audited by one or more properly qualified independent auditor(s) who who will be appointed by the Trustees.
deedKeyClauses.why: The deed requires an annual audit. It does not require publication of anything. This distinction matters: the absence of an FY2023-24 statement on the website establishes a publication gap, and does not by itself establish that no audit was done.
deedKeyClauses.transcriptionNote: The word 'who' is doubled in this transcription in error; the deed reads '...independent auditor(s) who will be appointed by the Trustees.'

deedKeyClauses.quote: No conditional Contributions shall be accepted.
The trusts of this Trust shall be and remain irrevocable for all times.

If the Board of Trustees decide to dissolve the Trust, the Trustees shall identify one or more public charitable trusts or institutions with objects similar to the Objects of the Trust and transfer the entire Trust Property to such public charitable trust or institutions ... and no part of the Trust Property shall be given to the Trustees or shall revert to the Settlor.

timeline.event: Press note by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru appealing for contributions establishes the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund. PMNRF has no trust deed; its genesis in a press note rather than an instrument is the fact both Delhi High Court judges in the 2018 appeal argue from.

Aseem Takyar applies to the CPIO, Prime Minister's Office for details of PMNRF transactions in FY2009-10 and FY2010-11. The CPIO supplies part and invokes section 8(1)(j) for the amount, name and particulars of each recipient, beneficiary and donor.
The Central Information Commission directs the CPIO to place details of PMNRF's institutional donors in the public domain. PMNRF files W.P.(C) 3897/2012 in the Delhi High Court.
Single Judge of the Delhi High Court dismisses PMNRF's writ petition, finding the CIC's order balanced, but expressly refrains from a conclusive finding on whether PMNRF is a public authority.

Delhi High Court Division Bench (S. Ravindra Bhat J and Sunil Gaur J) delivers a SPLIT verdict in LPA 231/2016, Prime Minister's National Relief Fund v. Aseem Takyar (reserved 21.09.2017, neutral citation 2018:DHC:3395-DB). Bhat J: PMNRF 'cannot but be called a public fund' and the appeal is dismissed. Gaur J: PMNRF 'is not a Public Authority within the definition of Section 2(h) of RTI Act and is thus, beyond its purview.' The question is referred to a third judge.

COVID-19 notified as a disaster for the purpose of assistance under the SDRF. The Supreme Court records at paragraph 71 that before this notification neither NDRF nor SDRF covered biological and public health emergencies.
e-Stamp certificate IN-DL40656151880688S issued to 'PM CARES', Rs 100, description 'Article 64 Trust'.
Deed of Trust executed at New Delhi by the Prime Minister of India as Settlor, creating a public charitable trust with an initial corpus of Rs 2,25,000. Witnesses Bhaskar Khulbe and Rajeev Topno.
Deed registered with Sub Registrar VII, New Delhi: Registration No. 163, Book No. 4, Vol No 1,685, pages 141 to 155. Executed and registered the same day.

PIB release from the Prime Minister's Office appeals for donations, states 'a public charitable trust ... has been set up. Prime Minister is the Chairman of this trust and its Members include Defence Minister, Home Minister and Finance Minister', and gives account and UPI details. Also the effective date from which contributions were later made eligible CSR expenditure.

The Ministry of Corporate Affairs conveys that contributions to PM CARES would be eligible as CSR activity under the Companies Act 2013. Established here from the government's own later answer in the Lok Sabha as reported; the MCA office memorandum itself could not be read (mca.gov.in 403s).
First accounting period closes. Rs 30,76,62,58,096 (Rs 3,076.63 cr) received in the five days from 27 to 31 March 2020, against total payments of Rs 2,049.

PM CARES Fund Trust announces its first allocation: Rs 3,100 cr, comprising approximately Rs 2,000 cr for 50,000 'Made-in-India' ventilators, Rs 1,000 cr for the welfare of migrants, and Rs 100 cr 'as a helping hand to catalyse vaccine development, which will be utilized under the supervision of Principal Scientific Advisor'.

Notification G.S.R. 313(E) inserts 'or Prime Minister's Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations Fund (PM CARES Fund)' into item (viii) of Schedule VII of the Companies Act 2013, with effect from 28 March 2020 - retrospective by 59 days. PMNRF was already named in item (viii). Established from the footnote to Schedule VII in India Code's official text of the Act.
SARC & Associates sign the FY2019-20 Receipts and Payments Account (UDIN 20084884AAAAAA1274). 100 days after the year end - the fastest of the four.

Supreme Court (Ashok Bhushan, R. Subhash Reddy, M.R. Shah JJ) decides W.P.(C) 546/2020, Centre for Public Interest Litigation v. Union of India. Refuses to direct transfer of PM CARES funds to the NDRF. Holds at paragraph 67 that 'The PM CARES Fund is a public charitable trust and is not a Government fund', and at paragraph 70 that 'for public charitable trust there is no occasion for audit by the Comptroller & Auditor General of India.' The Court did NOT decide whether PM CARES is a public authority under the RTI Act; that question was not before it.

In the Monsoon Session of the 17th Lok Sabha, the Minister of State for Finance and Corporate Affairs answers 'No sir' to an unstarred question by Shri Sunil Dattatray Tatkare asking whether the fund, having been set up on 27 March 2020 by the Central Government, is thereby a public authority under section 2(h) of the RTI Act. Asked about the retrospective amendment of Schedule VII, the Ministry answered: 'The Ministry on 28.03.2020 conveyed that contribution made to PM CARES Fund would be eligible as CSR activity under the Companies Act, 2013 and subsequently, issued a gazette notification to this effect'. The question number, exact answer date and the answer PDF could not be retrieved - see gaps.G06.

PM CARES Fund Trust allocates Rs 201.58 cr for 162 dedicated PSA Medical Oxygen Generation Plants, capacity 154.19 MT across 32 States/UTs, procurement through Central Medical Supply Store (CMSS). Rs 137.33 cr supply and commissioning plus CMSS management fee, Rs 64.25 cr Comprehensive Annual Maintenance Contract.

PM CARES gives 'in-principle approval' for 551 further PSA oxygen plants at district-headquarters government hospitals, procurement through the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The release states no rupee figure.

PM CARES for Children announced, covering children who lost both parents, the surviving parent, legal guardian or adoptive parents to COVID-19 from 11 March 2020. Lump sum Rs 10 lakh on attaining 23 years of age, monthly stipend from 18.

The Union files an affidavit in the Delhi High Court in the petitions of Samyak Gangwal, stating that PM CARES can be listed neither as 'the State' under Article 12 of the Constitution nor as a 'public authority' under the RTI Act, and that amounts in PM CARES are not transferred to the Consolidated Fund of India. Read from Scroll's report of the affidavit; the affidavit and the case record were not retrieved - see gaps.G04.
Ministry of Women and Child Development issues detailed guidelines for PM CARES for Children. Enrolment window 11.03.2020 to 31.12.2021, later extended.
SARC & Associates sign the FY2020-21 Receipts and Payments Account (UDIN 22084884AAAAAA2509 as handwritten). 286 days after the year end.

The Central Information Commission directs the CPIO of the Income Tax Department to provide documents submitted by PM CARES in its exemption application, and the file notings granting approval, to RTI applicant Girish Mittal. Order date established from the report of the judgment that later set it aside.

Prime Minister chairs a meeting of the Board of Trustees. Justice K.T. Thomas, Kariya Munda and Ratan Tata join as nominated trustees; Rajiv Mehrishi (former Comptroller and Auditor General of India), Sudha Murthy and Anand Shah are nominated to a new Advisory Board. The presentation records PM CARES for Children 'supporting 4345 children'.
SARC & Associates sign the FY2021-22 Receipts and Payments Account (UDIN 22084884AXGCSU1642). 183 days after the year end.

SARC & Associates sign the PMNRF FY2022-23 Receipts and Payments Account (UDIN 23084884BHBOMF2780). 182 days after the year end. This file is uploaded to pmnrf.gov.in on 23 December 2024 per its filename - 268 days after signature.

Delhi High Court (Subramonium Prasad J) sets aside the CIC order of 27.04.2022 in CPIO/Dy Commissioner of Income Tax (HQ Exemption), New Delhi v. Girish Mittal, holding that the CIC has no jurisdiction to direct furnishing of information covered by section 138 of the Income Tax Act. Judgment not retrieved - see gaps.G04.
SARC & Associates sign the FY2022-23 Receipts and Payments Account (UDIN 24084884BKIKDZ2614). 364 days after the year end - the slowest of the four, and the last statement PM CARES has published.
PMNRF's About page is last updated, per the page itself. Its ten-year table ends at FY2022-23.

Reported that the Prime Minister's Office has told the Lok Sabha Secretariat that questions on PM CARES, PMNRF and the National Defence Fund are inadmissible, citing Rules 41(2)(viii) and 41(2)(xvii) of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, on the ground that the funds are voluntary and receive nothing from the Consolidated Fund of India. Rule 41 is the same rule Gaur J relied on in his 2018 dissent to conclude that PMNRF is not a public authority. The PMO communication itself was not retrieved and its date is not established - see gaps.G08.

pmcares.gov.in About and FAQ pages last updated. The About page still indexes four Receipts and Payments Accounts, FY2019-20 to FY2022-23. FAQ Q19 names KKC & Associates LLP, Mumbai as the auditors appointed for 3 years.

positionA.holder: The Trust, the Prime Minister's Office and the Union of India
positionA.statement: It is not. The trust instrument itself recites that the Trust 'is not created by or under the Constitution of India or by any law made by the Parliament or by any State Legislature', is 'neither intended to be or is in fact owned, controlled or substantially financed by any Government or any instrumentality of the Government', and that the ex officio composition of the Board 'is merely for administrative convenience'. The Union told the Delhi High Court by affidavit on 14 September 2021 that the fund can be listed neither as 'the State' under Article 12 nor as a 'public authority' under the RTI Act, and that its amounts are not transferred to the Consolidated Fund of India. The Minister of State for Finance and Corporate Affairs answered 'No sir' in the Lok Sabha to the proposition that the fund's creation by the Central Government made it a public authority.
positionA.tier: documented for the deed clause; reported for the affidavit and the parliamentary answer

positionB.holder: RTI applicants and petitioners; and, on the analogous fund, S. Ravindra Bhat J
positionB.statement: On the closest judicial reasoning available - Bhat J on PMNRF - 'whilst PMNRF does not receive funding from the Central or State Governments, yet, it is administered in the office of the Prime Minister in accordance with the policy which exists in the public domain ... All those seconded to the office of the fund are public servants; they have no personal stake or interest. Such a fund cannot but be called as a public fund.' Bhat J also rejected the argument that the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha rules of procedure, or the absence of CAG audit, could bar disclosure, because 'Section 22 of the RTI Act overrides all other laws'. Applied to PM CARES the same facts hold: the PM chairs it, three Union ministers are ex officio trustees, the PMO provides its administration, its officers administer it in their official capacity, it operates on a gov.in domain whose footer reads '(c) 2026 Prime Minister's Office', and its stated head office is the Prime Minister's Office.

departuresThatSurvive.departure: PMNRF refuses PSU money; PM CARES accepts PSU CSR. This is the mechanism behind the ~100% PSU base rate, and it is stated on the two funds' own websites in terms that cannot be reconciled.
departuresThatSurvive.pmnrf: 'PMNRF accepts only voluntary donations by individuals and institutions. Contributions flowing out of budgetary sources of Government or from the balance sheets of the public sector undertakings are not accepted.'
departuresThatSurvive.pmcares: 'PM CARES Fund accepts voluntary contributions by individuals/organizations as well as contributions as part of CSR from Companies/Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs). However, contributions flowing out of budgetary sources of the PSUs are not accepted.'
departuresThatSurvive.significance: PMNRF excludes PSU balance-sheet contributions entirely. PM CARES excludes only contributions from budgetary sources, and expressly admits PSU CSR - which comes off the balance sheet. The exclusion PMNRF applies is precisely the one PM CARES drops. This is a documented, sourced, load-bearing difference between the two funds and, on the searching done here, it has not been assembled anywhere as the explanation for the PSU donation base rate.
departuresThatSurvive.innocentReading: PMNRF's rule dates from an era before section 135 CSR existed as a statutory levy. Once CSR became a 2% statutory obligation with a defined list of permitted destinations, a fund that refused CSR money would simply be refusing money that companies are compelled to spend somewhere. Admitting CSR is the ordinary consequence of being on Schedule VII, not evidence of design.

departuresThatSurvive.departure: PMNRF has no trust deed. PM CARES has one, and the section 2(h) test is recited in it in the negative.
departuresThatSurvive.significance: PMNRF's genesis is a press note of 24 January 1948, which is why both judges in the 2018 appeal had to argue from a website 'Preamble' rather than an instrument. PM CARES's instrument, executed and registered on 27 March 2020, contains at clause 5.3 an express recital tracking each limb of section 2(h): not created by the Constitution, not by any law of Parliament, not by any State Legislature, not owned, controlled or substantially financed by any Government, ex officio composition 'merely for administrative convenience'. Whether that was drafting prudence or anticipation is not something the record settles, and this file asserts nothing about it.
departuresThatSurvive.innocentReading: Any competent draftsman settling a public charitable trust in 2020 would recite non-governmental character, because the alternative is to leave the trust's legal characterisation to be litigated later. The recital is also, on its face, simply true of the funding: no budgetary support is received.

departuresThatSurvive.departure: Scale, and the speed of it.
departuresThatSurvive.significance: PM CARES received Rs 3,076.63 cr in the five days from 27 to 31 March 2020. PMNRF's total income for the whole of FY2019-20 was Rs 814.63 cr. PM CARES's five days exceed PMNRF's full year by 3.8x. In FY2020-21 PM CARES received Rs 7,913.55 cr against PMNRF's Rs 657.07 cr - 12.0x. PM CARES's closing balance at 31 March 2023, Rs 6,283.68 cr, exceeds PMNRF's Rs 5,956.50 cr, having existed for three years against PMNRF's seventy-five.

departuresThatSurvive.departure: Audit turnaround. PM CARES's audit lag went 100 days, 286 days, 183 days, 364 days. PMNRF's FY2022-23 statement was signed in 182 days.
departuresThatSurvive.significance: PMNRF, on the one comparable year, was audited in half the time. PM CARES's slowest year is its most recent published one.
departuresThatSurvive.innocentReading: PM CARES's FY2020-21 and FY2022-23 accounts carry many more transaction heads and more counterparties than PMNRF's, and 2020-22 was not an ordinary period for anyone's audit timetable.

control.verdict: The RTI-exemption position is a CONTINUATION, not a departure. It was asserted for PMNRF from 2011, litigated from 2012, and left unresolved by a split Delhi High Court verdict in 2018 - all before PM CARES existed. So is the absence of CAG audit, the withholding of the notes to the accounts, the choice of auditor, the administration by PMO officers on an honorary basis, and the halt in publication after FY2022-23. Commentary that presents any of these as PM CARES-specific is, on this record, wrong. What is genuinely specific to PM CARES is D1 (PSU CSR admitted where PMNRF refuses PSU balance-sheet money), D2 (the section 2(h) recital written into an instrument), D3 (scale) and D4 (audit turnaround).

csrEligibility.effect: Inserted 'or Prime Minister's Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations Fund (PM CARES Fund)' after 'Prime Minister's National Relief Fund' in item (viii) of Schedule VII of the Companies Act 2013.
csrEligibility.itemViiiAsAmended: contribution to the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund [or Prime Minister's Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations Fund (PM CARES Fund)] or any other fund set up by the Central Government for socio-economic development and relief and welfare of the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, other backward classes, minorities and women;
csrEligibility.sourceNote: Established from footnote 5 to Schedule VII in India Code's official consolidated text of the Companies Act 2013: 'Ins. by Notification No. G.S.R. 313(E), dated 26th May, 2020 (w.e.f. 28-03-2020).' The notification PDF itself is on mca.gov.in, which returns HTTP 403 to all automated fetching.
precisionCorrections: PMNRF was ALREADY in item (viii), inserted when the whole of items (i) to (x) were substituted by Notification G.S.R. 130(E) dated 27 February 2014 with effect from 1 April 2014. CSR eligibility for a Prime-Minister's relief fund is therefore not new and is not a PM CARES-specific concession. PM CARES was added to an existing entry.

The retrospective effect is real and precise: notified 26 May 2020, operative from 28 March 2020 - the day of the PIB donation appeal and the day after the trust deed was registered. Contributions made from 28 March 2020 were made CSR-eligible by an instrument issued 59 days later. The FY2019-20 voluntary contributions of Rs 3,075.85 cr were received in the window 27-31 March 2020, i.e. almost entirely inside the retrospective period.

The asymmetry that matters is central versus state, not PM CARES versus PMNRF. Item (viii) is confined to funds 'set up by the Central Government'. A Chief Minister's Relief Fund is not set up by the Central Government and is not a State Disaster Management Authority, so it falls in neither item (viii) nor item (xii). Item (xii), 'disaster management, including relief, rehabilitation and reconstruction activities', was inserted by Notification G.S.R. 390(E) dated 30 May 2019 with effect from 30 May 2019 - a year before COVID - and is the head under which contributions to State Disaster Management Authorities qualify. The exclusion of CM Relief Funds is therefore a consequence of the statutory text as it stood in 2019, not a discretionary carve-out created in 2020. That does not make the exclusion uncontroversial; it makes the common framing of it inaccurate.

The MCA's own account, given in answer to a Lok Sabha question and reported at the time: 'The Ministry on 28.03.2020 conveyed that contribution made to PM CARES Fund would be eligible as CSR activity under the Companies Act, 2013 and subsequently, issued a gazette notification to this effect'. So the administrative communication preceded the statutory instrument by 59 days, and the instrument was backdated to the communication.

PMNRF's foreign receipts are in its FAQ Q5 series, running Rs 27.88 lakh to Rs 245.04 lakh a year - against PM CARES's Rs 494.92 cr in FY2020-21 alone.

rejected.claim: PM CARES was created in order to escape the RTI Act.
rejected.killedBy: The control, and behind it the date test.
rejected.reason: The identical position - that a PMO-administered relief trust is not a 'public authority' under section 2(h) - was taken for PMNRF, a 1948 fund, in response to an RTI application in 2011, litigated by PMNRF from 2012, and left unresolved by a Delhi High Court Division Bench that split 1-1 on 23 May 2018. PM CARES did not exist until 27 March 2020. A position maintained in court for nine years before the entity existed cannot be the entity's purpose. The narrower claim - that the trust deed recites the section 2(h) test in the negative - survives and is recorded at control.departuresThatSurvive.D2, without any assertion about why.

rejected.claim: PM CARES's accounts have gone dark since FY2022-23, which is a PM CARES-specific failure.
rejected.reason: PMNRF's published series stops at exactly the same year. Both funds have published 4 of 7 elapsed financial years as at 2026-08-12. The base rate among comparable entities is 100%, which per the tiering table makes the property non-discriminating. What survives, and is recorded, is the quantified lag: 864 days outstanding against a worst previous turnaround of 364 days - for both funds.

rejected.claim: The trust deed was amended after execution to insert the 'no governmental control' recital.
rejected.reason: The recital is clause 5.3 of the instrument executed on 27 March 2020 and registered the same evening at pages 141 to 155 of Book 4. Nothing in the published PDF indicates an amendment. The second e-stamp of 11 May 2020 is unexplained and is recorded as gap G09 rather than as evidence for a theory it does not support.

rejected.claim: Ratan Tata's nomination as a trustee in September 2022 is connected to corporate contributions to the fund.
rejected.killedBy: No primary record, and the date test in any case.
rejected.reason: No document read here records any contribution by any Tata entity to PM CARES - the fund publishes no donor names at all - and the nomination postdates the fund's peak inflow period by about 29 months. This is adjacency, not a link. It is a hypothesis for the pattern-prospector, not a finding, and it is named here so that it is visibly declined rather than silently omitted.

rejected.claim: The auditor's political sympathies bear on the audit.
rejected.reason: An allegation of this kind appears in at least one outlet. It was not read, it concerns an individual's political views rather than a documented act, and this desk does not publish allegations about individuals without the primary record and the response. Declined outright. The auditor facts that ARE recorded here are those printed on documents the Government itself publishes: firm name, firm registration number, partner name, membership number, UDIN and signature date - and the material point about them is comparative, that the same firm audits PMNRF.

rejected.claim: PM CARES's use of the State Emblem and the gov.in domain is unlawful.
rejected.reason: The observable facts are recorded - the fund operates at pmcares.gov.in and its pages carry the footer '(c) 2026 Prime Minister's Office' - and they belong in contested C3 as evidence on the control question. The legal claim requires the Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act 1950, the domain-allotment policy, and any order on the point, none of which were retrieved. Downgraded from a claim to an observation.

rejected.claim: The Supreme Court settled that PM CARES is outside the RTI Act.
rejected.reason: W.P.(C) 546/2020 decides three questions, numbered 3, 4 and 5, all about the National Disaster Response Fund and the Disaster Management Act 2005. Section 2(h) of the RTI Act is not mentioned in it. The characterisation at paragraph 67 - 'a public charitable trust and ... not a Government fund' - is made in that statutory context. Both sides of the public argument cite this judgment for a proposition it does not contain.

rejected.claim: PM CARES received Rs 10,990 cr in FY2020-21.
rejected.killedBy: Reading the statement rather than its bottom line.
rejected.reason: Rs 10,990.17 cr is the printed 'Total' line, which includes the Rs 3,076.63 cr opening balance brought forward. FY2020-21 receipts alone are Rs 7,913.55 cr. Every published year's 'Total' line includes the opening balance; adding the four Total lines together double-counts three opening balances.
